newsitem.title: INDIA: India castor market closed for Buddhist holiday.
newsitem.headline: India castor market closed for Buddhist holiday.

text.p: The castorseed forward market was officially closed in Bombay on Thursday to mark the birth anniversary of Lord Buddha.
"No trading took place in the kerb deals amid very poor attendance among the operators as banks were closed for the holiday," a dealer said.

"Even when the market remains officially open, the volume of trading nowadays is very slow following introduction of daily clearing by the exchange authorities and today no kerb deals took place," he added.
Groundnut oil held steady at the reduced level of 355/357 rupees per 10 kg amid limited arrivals of 40/50 tonnes but physical buying remained at a low ebb.
"Arrivals of summer crop in producing centres slowed down due to the peak in the marriage season and farmers were busy attending marriages in producing centres," a broker said.
"Arrivals will pick up again as soon as the marriages are over," he added.
In Rajkot spot groundnut oil was steady at 559/560 rupees per 15 kg.

"In Bombay imported palm-oil remained steady at the reduced level of 279/280 rupees per 10 kg but traders were expecting modest rally from the current level looking at increased outstation enquiries from bulk consumers," one importer said.
"Palm-oil may bounce back from this level," he added.
